newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian parties retain seats in by-elections.
newsitem.headline: Indian parties retain seats in by-elections.

text.p: The Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party, the centre-left Janata Dal and a communist-backed independent have each won a seat in parliamentary by-elections, state radio said on Sunday.
The results of the May 29 by-elections make no difference to the balance of power in the 545-member lower house of parliament, Lok Sabha.

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal, which heads the ruling United Front coalition, won the Aska seat in the eastern state of Orissa, vacant since the death in April of veteran nationalist Biju Patnaik. His son, Naveen, won the seat.
The BJP's Lal Bihari Tiwari won the East Delhi seat, vacated by a BJP resignation.
An independent, Sebastian Paul, won the Ernakulam seat in the southern state of Kerala, vacated by the death of Xavier Arakal, who was also an independent backed by the communist-led Left Front.
The BJP has 163 seats and the 15-party United Front 178 seats in the Lok Sabha. The Congress party, which offers vital support to the United Front to keep out the BJP, has 140 seats.
